articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang Gets Hero’s Welcome Upon Return To Nvidia HQ, Video Shows
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang Gets Hero’s Welcome Upon Return To Nvidia HQ, Video Shows
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO , effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.
The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk."
President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard."
Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.
Shares of Nvidia surged 33% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6.
"I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process."
Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That update prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people said.
Huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations.
Trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump said the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."
He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."
"On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote.
Several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX , Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected."
Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
For weeks following Huang's ouster, the company's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it."
"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company."
Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China.
Lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips.
"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., said in a statement Monday.
Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his plans to testify.
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., said Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls."
"Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday.

articles.title_orig: Why Anthropic’s Stock Is Sitting Out Nvidia’s Big Rally
articles.title_zh: Why Anthropic’s Stock Is Sitting Out Nvidia’s Big Rally
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Just two days after its public debut, the stock market's newest AI giant, Anthropic ( ANT ), looks to be missing out on Monday's major tech rally.
The stock of the Claude model maker fell 1.4% on Monday, trading below $88 as of 3:00 p.m. ET after whipsawing earlier in the day. Meanwhile, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and other AI-linked stocks, including CoreWeave ( CRWV ), soared amid the broader tech rebound that followed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.
The move comes after Anthropic's stock sank 9% on Friday following a 17% gain on its IPO day last Thursday. At Monday's current price, the stock is up about 5% from its $83 IPO price.
Read more: What investors should know about buying into Anthropic stock
The choppy performance might reflect ordinary post IPO profit-taking and broader skepticism about Anthropic's valuation. Needham analysts said in a Sunday note that the most common concern they hear from investors is whether the company can sustain its enormous revenue growth next year. The company's fully diluted IPO valuation of about $1.5 trillion is roughly 40 times trailing sales.
The stock also has a potential supply overhang. As much as 315 million shares held by insiders, roughly one-third of the stock the company issued in its IPO, became eligible for sale almost immediately, according to Anthropic's IPO paperwork.
Needham added that given Anthropic's staggered schedule for permitting insider share sales could bring more shares to market in the first six months.
Another key question hanging over the company is how credit markets will absorb the AI firm's massive spending needs. Anthropic has committed to spending about $900 billion on its computing and infrastructure needs for the next two decades , including $70 billion due over the next 12 months.
The AI boom's ravenous capital needs have flooded the bond market this year, becoming a looming concern for investors.
Investors expect the major rating agencies to assign a high-yield, or junk, rating to the company's debt, according to a Wall Street Journal report . No rating has yet been announced.
Anthropic's credit rating is key for the wider AI ecosystem. Getting the higher investment-grade rating would help offer some relief to chip makers, including Nvidia and Broadcom ( AVGO ), that have guaranteed billions of dollars worth of microchips to customers that lease compute power to major model makers like Anthropic and rival OpenAI. ( OPAI.PVT )
The high-yield bond market also comes with constraints, including smaller capacity and higher borrowing rates, for the newly public giant.

articles.title_orig: New York judge urged Kalshi to compromise on limiting bets by anyone under 21
articles.title_zh: New York judge urged Kalshi to compromise on limiting bets by anyone under 21
articles.content_orig:
A New York judge on Monday urged Kalshi to reach a compromise limiting bets on sports and culture contracts by anyone younger than 21 years old while denying a temporary restraining order that risked shutting down the prediction market across all 50 states.
The potential compromise was raised during a hearing when a state judge heard arguments over the New York attorney general’s claims that Kalshi is operating an illegal gambling platform by failing to obtain a state gambling license, not paying taxes, and allowing users below the legal betting age to participate. The state is seeing a temporary restraining order to shut down Kalshi from offering bets within or from New York.
Young adults under 21 traded $5 billion on Kalshi this year, amid prediction market frenzy
Judge Melissa Crane said she was “very concerned” about the risks to people under 21 years old, who under state law are banned from gambling. Kalshi allows anyone 18 years old and up to use their platform.
“Would your client be willing, at least in New York, to stop these (contracts or bets) for 18- to 21-year-olds just to have a compromise at this point?” she asked.
“We are open to engaging” on 18- to 20-year-olds issue,” said Grant Mainland, a lawyer for Kalshi. He said they could work out a form of “interim compliance” during the litigation as it relates to sports and culture contracts. He added Kalshi has a number of consumer protections already in place.
The judge is giving both sides until Monday, November 30, to reach a deal.
“I would like the parties to discuss a way of safeguarding for that age group ultimately,” she said.
Crane told the NYAG’s office she was denying the TRO request because “You’re really seeking the ultimate relief in the case upfront without me even hearing from the defense. It seems to me I’d be reversed in a minute if I issued the full TRO that you want.”
She said she was also concerned about a broader market disruption if all bets on Kalshi were frozen.
Mainland told the judge a TRO is a “recipe for chaos” and would put millions of people at risk by freezing their trades. “It would be a market emergency. A sudden shut down of that would be totally unprecedented.”
Brent Tomer, an attorney for the NYAG’s office, defended the need for a TRO, saying betting on Kalshi has exploded since the New York gaming commission first sent a cease-and-desist letter in September 2025. Kalshi’s valuation went from $5 billion to $40 billion and the volume of contracts is now $118 billion, up from $5 billion over the same period, he said.
“Eighty-five percent of that on their platform relates to sport betting,” Tomer said.
The judge said she would set an expedited schedule with briefs due over the next few weeks and a hearing in early January.
The decision comes against the backdrop of a broader debate within the courts over whether prediction market platforms fall exclusively under the oversight of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission or are subject to state gaming laws. The Supreme Court has been petitioned to resolve the split.
After the hearing, a spokesperson for Kalshi said, “The judge denied the State’s request for a TRO, recognizing that there are complex questions about derivatives and preemption. We remain committed to working with the State on a path forward that works for our 1.5 million customers and for the state of New York.”
CNN has a partnership with Kalshi and uses its data to cover major events. But CNN editorial employees are not allowed to use prediction markets.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang may be back but the China hawks probably haven't given up
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang may be back but the China hawks probably haven't given up
articles.content_orig:
Charles Gasparino is out with an interesting report. He argues that the Nvidia saga isn't over and for reasons that could rattle the equity bulls.
The drama is no surprise but this is a concern:
Now it's not clear that "stuff that is coming out" means news we already know about or conjecture but it's a reminder that there are powerful forces that don't like how Nvidia has behaved and don't want to see Huang succeed. Now maybe it's China hawks in a power play and they've now had their wings clipped or maybe the people fighting against open source AI really want to take Huang down.
So now we just have to wait for the next round of leaks. No one likes to hear about accounting leaks and the vendor finance is a real problem.
Shares are up 30% today but they've flatlined from the open. When people hear about accounting issues, they're inclined to take some off the table.

articles.title_zh: Poland to get NATO early-warning aircraft after Russian missiles hit country
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez to resign after Ethics Committee finds he engaged in sexual misconduct
NATO will deploy an AWACS early-warning system aircraft to Poland as part of its response to ⁠three missiles landing in the country on the military alliance’s eastern flank, a Polish deputy defense minister said on Monday.
Three Russian Kh-101 missiles ⁠landed in Poland ​on ⁠Friday, prosecutors said, adding to fears that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spill ⁠into NATO territory.
“An AWACS early-warning aircraft ​will ⁠be made available to Poland,” ‌ Pawel Zalewski told reporters after a NATO meeting in Brussels. “This is a very ‌good system that gives us ‌even deeper... operational awareness which allows us to respond better to this kind of threat.”
With their distinctive ⁠nine-meter-wide radar domes, NATO’s 14 Airborne Warning and Control System aircraft have served as the alliance’s eyes in the sky since 1982.
Based at Geilenkirchen air base in Germany, the fleet has played an important role ‌in surveillance missions along NATO’s eastern ​flank since Russia launched its ‌full-scale invasion of Ukraine in ⁠2022.
In a conflict, they can ⁠provide a common radar picture for allied fighters, ships ‌and control ​centers, while directing NATO combat ‌jets to their ​targets.

articles.title_orig: Senate schedules Jensen Huang hearing
articles.title_zh: Senate schedules Jensen Huang hearing
articles.content_orig:
NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, D-Calif., about congressional efforts to question Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about China's access to Nvidia chips.
For more, we're joined now by Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove. She represents California's 37th Congressional District in LA and serves on the House Foreign Relations Committee. She's the top Democrat on the subcommittee on South and Central Asia with jurisdiction over export control, and she and a few of her colleagues say they want some answers from U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Good morning, Congresswoman. Thank you for joining us.
SYDNEY KAMLAGER-DOVE: Good morning. Thanks for having me.
FADEL: Now, you and two of your Democratic colleagues, Jamie Raskin and Gregory Meeks, are asking for more information to determine whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick blocked efforts to restrict Chinese access to Nvidia chips. Lay out your concerns here and what you are looking for.
KAMLAGER-DOVE: Yeah. So the commerce secretary is responsible for protecting our money and our national security. And we think the American people deserve to know if he is doing that, or if he is putting his family's financial interests ahead of our national security. This smells like corruption, and it actually smells like an acute risk to this country's national security.
So we sent this letter because we have a lot of questions. We want to know was the decision to sell these chips to Megaspeed, was it influenced by Jensen Huang, who's a major Trump ally, who donated $25 million to Trump's ballroom? Was it because the commerce secretary's son's investment firm has hundreds of millions of dollars tied up in Nvidia, and that could be affected by the outcome of all of this case?
And we want to know how deep all of this goes. Where are the other implications? Because Howard Lutnick has been personally involved all of the decision-making around these chips deals, and he has been slow-walking rulemaking that would protect our country's national security and our assets like these chips.
FADEL: And you sent the letter to the head of the family firm that his son now runs, which he exited when he joined the Trump administration. I will note that the firm is saying they've done nothing wrong and will show that. Do you suspect that laws were broken?
KAMLAGER-DOVE: I definitely think that there are a lot of backroom deals that have happened to allow companies like Nvidia to sell these kinds of chips to Megaspeed. You know, at one point, Cantor Fitzgerald actually owned 3.5 million shares of Nvidia. That's a lot. That's worth about $1.3 billion. And once the White House started investigating Megaspeed, A, Howard Lutnick asked all of this investigations - all of these investigations to be shifted to DOJ. And then also, Cantor Fitzgerald started divesting in those shares.
But we also know that these are very important chips. You know, they're really special. They run military. They run our banks, our water infrastructure, things like the NSA. And if these chips are getting into the wrong hands, if they're going to China, that puts our country at risk at the expense of the American people.
FADEL: What do you see as the appropriate limits to put on the export of these semiconductor chips?
KAMLAGER-DOVE: Well, we have been asking all of these questions for over a year, and there has been so little traction with this last Congress. And we've said, If you have some of these bad actors that are on these do-not-sell lists, why are you finding ways to work around those lists so that companies can sell to other companies that can then - and will - sell these chips to China?
It is a problem because once these chips leave our hands, we cannot get them back. And we are giving our adversaries the opportunity to catch up with us and advance our technologies and put the American people in harm's way. We need a much more robust rulemaking system, and we need secretaries that will adhere to those laws rather than finding a way to work around them, either to put Americans at risk or to make money for themselves and Trump's inner circle.
FADEL: Republican Senator Tim Scott, who chairs the Senate banking committee, formally invited Lutnick to appear for a public hearing next month on Nvidia and chip exports. Does that give you confidence in a thorough bipartisan inquiry here?
KAMLAGER-DOVE: I hope so. National security is a bipartisan issue, and we should all be motivated to want to get to the bottom of this and to stop this from happening. This is costing Americans money, and at some point, we could be costing Americans' lives. And I would hope that Republicans and Democrats could stand together and say no more of this.
FADEL: Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove is the ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia. Thank you for joining us.
KAMLAGER-DOVE: Thank you so much.

articles.title_orig: Captain who abandoned passengers on sinking Costa Concordia cruise ship released early from prison
articles.title_zh: Captain who abandoned passengers on sinking Costa Concordia cruise ship released early from prison
articles.content_orig:
Francesco Schettino, the former captain of the Costa Concordia, which shipwrecked off the coast of Italy, has been released from prison early after serving 9 years of a 16-year sentence for manslaughter.
After nine years in a Rome prison , the captain of the Costa Concordia, Francesco Schettino, was released early from prison. Italian newspaper Quotidiano Nazionale reports he will serve the remaining 7 years of his 16-year sentence for manslaughter on supervised probation.
Schettino’s lawyer, Francesca Carnicelli, told Fox News, "I can confirm that Mr. Schettino is currently finishing his sentence under a program that allows him to live outside of prison," saying, "he has a job as an office worker, must be home by 10:00 p.m. and is not allowed to leave the province where he resides."
CRUISE COMPANY FOUNDER SAYS HE'S 'THE VILLAIN' AFTER 200-PLUS PASSENGERS ARE STRANDED
Francesco Schettino, former captain of the shipwrecked Costa Concordia, was released early from prison after serving 9 years of a 16-year sentence for abandoning his ship before it was fully evacuated. (Laura Lezza/Getty Images)
Almost 15 years ago, on Jan. 13, 2012, the Costa Concordia slammed into rocks off Tuscany’s Giglio island. Schettino reportedly veered off course to perform a "sail-by salute." There were 4,200 passengers and crew on board, and 32 people were killed.
Schettino faced backlash after abandoning the ship , while hundreds of passengers were waiting to be rescued. At the time, Schettino told Italian La Repubblica that while helping others he tripped and ended up in one of the lifeboats.
'THIS WAS A MIRACLE': CRUISE PASSENGERS DESCRIBE FRANTIC ESCAPE AS TANKER STRIKES SHIP
The Costa Concordia cruise ship lies capsized off the shore of the island of Giglio, Italy, on January 14, 2012. More than four thousand people were on board when the ship struck a rock. (MAURIX/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images)
A Netflix documentary titled, "Shipwrecked: Nightmare at Sea," was released earlier this year.
American Nicholas Taliaferro, who survived the tragedy, told Fox News, "We have an opportunity to ask ourselves, a very important question was justice truly served? and that question is not only for those watching the documentary, but especially the victims and the survivors and the families who have had to live the consequences of the captain and everybody else that was involved for nearly 15 years, because serving a sentence and delivering justice aren’t necessarily the same thing."
JULY 17, 2013: COURT HEARS HOW 32 DIED IN COSTA CONCORDIA SHIPWRECK
The Costa Concordia struck rocks off Tuscany's Giglio island in Italy on January 13, 2012, after Francesco Schettino veered off course to perform a "sail-by salute." The crash killed 32 of the 4,200 passengers and crew on board. (Target Presse Agentur Gmbh/Getty Images)
Prosecutors argued the captain was cowardly in his actions and refused the Italian Coast Guard’s orders to go back onboard and help with the evacuation.

Taliaferro said: "Whether you’re in United States or in Italy, or anywhere, the captain is the last one to get off the boat and he was the first one and now you’re the first one to get out, I mean it just seems a little disrespectful to the families and the survivors".
Stephanie Bennett currently serves as a London-based reporter for Fox News Channel (FNC).

articles.title_orig: My approach to EU is pragmatic, says Burnham
articles.title_zh: My approach to EU is pragmatic, says Burnham
articles.content_orig:
The prime minister has said new agreements with the EU are "pragmatic" and "not a prelude to anything", as he outlined his agreement with the bloc to MPs.
Andy Burnham told the Commons there was "no fixed destination" on talks to explore closer ties with the European Union, adding it would be "unthinkable" for the UK to rejoin the bloc without a referendum.
After several former prime ministers urged him to not reopen the Brexit debate, Burnham said they are "stuck in the past" - and later claimed there would be "no banging on about Europe" from Labour.
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said Burnham has "oversold" the deal and was "trying to take Britain back to 2015".
At a summit on Friday, Burnham agreed a new deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.
He also finalised the latest stage of the government's post-Brexit "reset" of relations with the EU and said both sides will "brainstorm" options for their long-term relationship.
He has previously suggested potential options for the future could include rejoining the customs union, the single market or a fresh referendum on full EU membership.
However, he has ruled out major changes to the UK-EU relationship before the next general election, saying he will stick to Labour's 2024 manifesto pledge not to return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement.
Speaking in the Commons on Monday, Conservative MP Sir Edward Leigh said the "reset" with the EU is "a prelude to the prime minister's sincere desire to rejoin the EU and have another referendum" and risked leading to another Scottish independence referendum.
Burnham replied to the Gainsborough MP: "It's not a prelude to anything. It's a pragmatic approach and it will continue to be a pragmatic approach.
"If it's in Britain's national interest, I will recommend it to this House. If it is not, then I won't. There is no fixed opinion here. There is no fixed destination.
"Europe could change again in the next year, 18 months, and we'll have to obviously watch how life changes. But where Britain can make progress, surely we should make progress."
The prime minister also told MPs the government's forthcoming 10-year plan for the country will consider the "range of options for our long-term relationship with our largest market" - the EU.
MPs heard the "plan for Britain" will be published next month and the results of the "informal exchanges of ideas" with the EU will be presented around the time of their next joint summit.
To laughter from the opposition benches, Burnham said: "So there will be no banging on about Europe from this side or a running commentary."
The words echoed those used by Conservative former Prime Minister Lord Cameron in 2006 .
Burnham went on to say there would be a "calm, constructive and pragmatic consideration of what is in Britain's interests in the long-term", adding "always the British people will be the boss and they will decide what comes next".
Conservative MP Sir Bernard Jenkin asked Burnham to "give a clear and unequivocal statement that it would be unthinkable for any prime minister to try and take the UK back into the EU without a referendum".
Burnham replied to the Harwich and North Essex MP : "Yes, it would be unthinkable."
Speaking for the Opposition, Badenoch said Burnham's EU deal "wasn't really about reducing the cost of living" but instead "committing Britain to becoming a rule taker from Brussels, something he had no mandate to do".
Badenoch also said: "Six former prime ministers, including Tony Blair, are criticising the direction he is taking UK-EU relations. He says the prime ministers who implemented a democratic decision are living in the past.
"The only person living in the past is the man trying to take Britain back to 2015 instead of focusing on the future."
Over the weekend, Baroness May, who spent three years negotiating an EU exit deal, told the BBC she was "aghast" Burnham could be considering rejoining.
She urged him to "accept Brexit and move on".
Rishi Sunak has also warned against reopening the "divisive" debate about rejoining the EU, telling Sky News it would be "a huge distraction for government".
Earlier this month, Boris Johnson, who negotiated the original Brexit deal as prime minister, said it was "madness" for Burnham to make Brexit his "political priority".
He told the Daily Telegraph , he believed the public would back Brexit again if Burnham forced another vote on the issue.
His predecessor Lord Cameron, who resigned as prime minister after losing the 2016 Brexit referendum, has also warned against "another-decade long debate about whether we should be in or out".
Meanwhile, former Labour Prime Minister Sir Tony - who was a prominent opponent of leaving the EU - has said the UK should only rejoin the bloc if it reforms and allows more innovation on technology.
Asked about the criticism from his predecessors, Burnham earlier told broadcasters: "They're stuck in the past because they can't face up to the bad deal that they did."
He added: "I'm not a prime minister that's going to be stuck in the past."
Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey welcomed the new agreements before telling the Commons that a "totally new deal for Britain" is needed now.
Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice labelled it a "terrible" deal, while Green Party MP Ellie Chowns said "bold and brave politics, not baby steps" are needed.

articles.title_orig: Apple Prepares to Launch Product(Red) HomePod Mini and AirPods Max
articles.title_zh: Apple Prepares to Launch Product(Red) HomePod Mini and AirPods Max
articles.content_orig:
When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn't affect our editorial independence .
Apple has a longstanding tradition of supporting the Product(RED) cause, in which manufacturers create products in a very specific red color scheme, with a portion of the proceeds from those products go toward international charities that fight HIV and AIDS. However, it’s been a while since Apple sold a product in a Product(RED) colorway, and we assumed the partnership had run its course.
That’s not the case. Bloomberg reports that on or around December 1, Apple will introduce two new Product (RED) products for the first time in years. They will be the AirPods Max 2 , in silver with a red digital crown, and an all-red HomePod mini 2. While Apple previously sold a silver version of the AirPods Max, the latest version released in April does not include a silver option.
The Product(RED) campaign was started in 2006 by Bono and Bobby Shriver, and Apple was one of the first companies on board. It has been several years since the last Product(RED) offering from Apple: 2022’s iPhone 14 and 2023’s Apple Watch Series 9 were the last to be offered in Product(RED). A few iPhone cases were available for a short time after that.
Product(RED) Apple products don’t cost more than any other color, and these should be on shelves in time for the holidays. So if you like red, hold off on buying a new Homepod mini or AirPods Max for another week.
Jason has written about technology over 25 years - first in the gaming press, then focusing on enthusiast PCs and general technology. He enjoys learning how complicated technology works and explaining it in a way anyone can understand.

articles.title_orig: Amazon’s China-made adult bed rails recalled after 89-year-old woman dies of suffocation
articles.title_zh: Amazon’s China-made adult bed rails recalled after 89-year-old woman dies of suffocation
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of adult bed rails from China that were sold in the US have been recalled after an 89-year-old woman died of suffocation when she was trapped between the product and her mattress.
About 2,114 adult bed rails sold on Amazon by Guangzhou Yupin Technology Co. – a Chinese company doing business as Xentrawave – are included in the recall, according to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission.
All batches of Xentrawave’s model XT016 and batch number 20251212 of model XT026 are included in the recall for failing to meet mandatory safety requirements, because customers can be pinned between the rail and the side of the mattress – posing a risk of death by asphyxiation.
The XT106 model adult bed rail also doesn’t meet structural stability requirements and its push pins and push pin holes are incorrectly sized, posing a risk of laceration, the agency said.
The CPSC said it has received one report of a death related to the Xentrawave recall, involving the 89-year-old woman who died from asphyxiation.
Customers can find the model numbers XT016 or XT026 on the front of the product’s outer packaging and the first page of the instruction manual.
For the XT026 model, consumers can locate the batch number on the product label attached to the back of the bed rail’s gray fabric pouch and in the instruction manual.
Consumers should immediately stop use of the recalled bed rails and contact Xentrawave for a full refund.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
They will be asked to cut the foam padding on the bed rail handles, disassemble the product and email a photo of the destroyed bed rail to xentrawavedirect@163.com or submit it online at https://xentrawahelp.com/xentrawave-bed-rail-safety-recall/ .
The recalled XT016 bed rails were sold on Amazon from May 2025 through March 2026 and the XT026 model was sold from March 2026 through August 2026. The bed rails cost between $37 and $40.
The bed rails were manufactured by China-based Guangzhou Nanyu Medical Technology Co.

articles.title_orig: Drone Attack Hits Colombian City as Unmanned Explosives Transform Conflict
articles.title_zh: Drone Attack Hits Colombian City as Unmanned Explosives Transform Conflict
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — Earlier this month, drones flew over a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, in Colombia’s Bolívar department, dropping explosives that killed three soldiers when detonated.
Just days before that in October, the Colombian military said a vessel assigned to Riverine Marine Battalion No. 42 was attacked in the Guapi River in a similar fashion, killing one Marine and injuring four others.
In September, a civilian radar in the Valle del Cauca region was damaged after what appeared to be an explosive-laden drone reportedly collided with it.
And a new attack occurred just this Saturday evening: the headquarters of a battalion in La Jagua de Ibirico, César department, were attacked with drones and explosives. One soldier died and at least 12 were wounded.
The incidents, analysts say, are the latest examples of militant groups operating drones in ways that mirror battlefield uses — leaving local governments to race to catch up with the technology needed to defend against them. And Colombia appears to be ground zero for what could emerged as a new wave of conflict against rebels and narco groups in South and Central America.
The explosive-carrying drones are “inexpensive, easy to acquire and useful for monitoring security forces and protecting illicit operations,” Rebecca Bill Chavez, former US deputy assistant secretary for defense for Western Hemisphere Affairs, told Breaking Defense.
Use of small drones by militant and drug-trafficking groups isn’t new, but Chavez, the president of the Inter American Dialogue, said a growing problem is that the groups “have gone from using drones to monitor troop movements to launching coordinated attacks with multiple drones,” including unmanned systems using fiber-optic guidance systems.
Expanding manufacturing capacity is critical to producing missiles, radars, and launch systems.
Colombia has emerged as the flash point since August, when a new government led by President Abelardo de la Espriella promised a “mano dura” — or strong hand — approach to countering cartel and other armed groups. The Colombian armed forces have carried out several major operations, including air strikes, against historic rebel groups like the ELN and FARC, as well as drug cartels like the Clan del Golfo, and other non-state criminal networks. (Each of the named groups have been declared a terrorist organization by the US State Department.)
In response, during just the first 100 days of de la Espriella’s term, Colombia has suffered at least 93 attacks that involved drones, according to country’s news agency Caracol Radio . Of the 26 Army personnel killed during these 100 days, “at least 11” were killed due to drone-dropped explosives. (Colombian insurgents generally do not take responsibility for drone attacks, with the government usually assigning blame.)
On Nov. 8 , the Ministry of Defense announced the seizure of a weapons cache, property of the Clan del Golfo, which included one drone and 35 grenades “conditioned to be dropped by this [uncrewed] aircraft,” suggesting that local insurgent groups are still investing in these weapons.
“There is no conventional drone warfare in Colombia,” a Colombian former army colonel told Breaking Defense on the condition of anonymity. “Rather, there are sporadic attacks against units in frontline areas which have no c-UAS [counter-unmanned aerial systems] protection.”
The surge in drone threats is likely to lead to greater investment in counter-drone systems.
The previous president, Gustavo Petro, announced Bogotá would create an “ anti-drone shield ” that would include fixed, mobile and man-portable counter-drone systems. But Colombia’s new defense minister, Jorge Eduardo Mora, said the effort hadn’t amounted to much by the time the new administration came in.
The Colombian armed forces do operate some counter-UAS systems. The Defense Ministry released photos of soldiers with jamming rifles on Nov. 8, stating that troops in the Chocó department had neutralized a drone to prevent “grenades from being dropped on soldiers.”
However, more systems are needed. The retired colonel explained to Breaking Defense that the armed forces require “air defense systems specifically for drone threats, both mobile and fixed.” Chavez agreed, saying “investing in counter-drone defenses is essential to protect soldiers, police, and civilians.”
One potential remedy, according to Henry Ziemer of the Americas Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, would be for Colombia to join the US-run drone and counter-drone marketplace , as Argentina, Mexico and Panama have reportedly done. In August, the US military sent out the first “tranche” of invitations to “selected international partners” with a second tranche to follow.
But relations between Washington and Bogotá may have become more complicated this month after The New York Times reported that de la Espriella had rebuffed an American offer of joint counter-drug operations — though de la Espriella denied the report . On Friday, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrapped up a Central and South American tour, praising the closeness of US and Colombian militaries.
Still, getting help with counter-drone capabilities from the US or elsewhere and training up Colombian soldiers is only “part of the answer,” Chavez said.
“Without stronger intelligence and investigative capabilities, governments will keep responding to attacks without stopping the criminal organizations behind them,” she said.
“Who is supplying and modifying these drones? Who is training the operators?” she asked. “The goal should be to dismantle those networks, not just shoot down drones once they’re airborne.”
The retired Colombian colonel, a Lancero, said he agreed. The Ministry of Defense and other agencies “need to strengthen intelligence operations to locate where the narco-insurgents’ drone bases are,” he said.
And it’s not just Colombia. So far, drones carrying lethal explosives have also been used in attacks in Brazil and Mexico . Ziemer is pessimistic about the future.
“As knowledge of drone tactics proliferates faster than governments deploy countermeasures, it seems likely we will begin to see them crop up in more countries in the region.”

articles.title_orig: Over 700,000 Russian Soldiers Have Died in Ukraine, Analysis Indicates
articles.title_zh: Over 700,000 Russian Soldiers Have Died in Ukraine, Analysis Indicates
articles.content_orig:
Meduza, Mediazona, and more than a dozen other journalistic teams will present the results of an independent analysis of Russian mortality data tonight, after 5 p.m. CET . The data came from the hacker groups Cyber Partisans of Belarus and SilentCrow, who obtained it after hacking Rosstat’s database.
We and colleagues from other independent outlets spent more than two weeks examining the leak, verifying its authenticity and searching the records Rosstat received from the EGR ZAGS for data on losses among Russian troops since the start of the full-scale war.
All the journalists who worked on this project concluded that the database is largely authentic. Final loss estimates may vary between outlets, depending on how each includes or excludes certain categories of the dead. Not every death can be definitively linked to combat operations, even using the leak’s detailed cause-of-death data. As a result, estimates of Russian military losses vary depending on how that link is interpreted and on the nuances of counting. We will explain in detail why we are confident our own count is accurate.
The EGR ZAGS data in the leak include only registered deaths. For military personnel, the delay between death and registration can run six months or longer, and the share of these late registrations has been growing. As a result, a significant share of the dead are missing even from Rosstat’s internal data, especially over the past year and a half.
Estimating the true number of Russian military losses, accounting for these late registrations, therefore requires research that draws not only on the EGR ZAGS leak but also on many other independently obtained data sets and statistical modeling. Meduza will publish an estimate of these “invisible” deaths alongside its analysis of the Rosstat leak.
At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication.

NVDA rose 5.8% in overnight trading after dropping 23% in the week, its worst weekly drop since September 2008.
Retail sentiment was 'extremely bullish' for NVDA, 'bullish' for AMD, MU and SNDK, 'bearish' for INTC and SOXX.
AI giant Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq on Thursday after a blockbuster IPO, but the stock lost steam after the opening-day rally.
Tech stocks rebounded sharply in Sunday's overnight trading after a challenging week, as concerns over AI overvaluation appeared to outweigh optimism around Anthropic's (ANT) landmark IPO and another strong quarterly report from Nvidia (NVDA).
Tech analysts such as Dan Ives said that while "bears will feel validation," there is no stopping the AI revolution and that there were "clear areas of safety/winners despite the noise and market backdrop worries."
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
NVDA stock rose 5.8% in overnight trading after dropping 23% in the week, its worst weekly drop since September 2008. Intel (INTC) gained 4.8%, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) climbed 5.4%. Memory stocks also rallied, with Micron Technology (MU) up 4.6% and SanDisk (SNDK) advancing 5.2%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) rose 4.2%.
"Yelling fire in a crowded theater moment is here and the bears will take center stage with this narrative and ultimately with Jensen out at Nvidia, market fears globally, and the Blue Tidal Wave in DC going after Big Tech this will be bumpy road over the coming months," Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said in an X post.
"That said, the technology age of AI is coming one way or another…and this is not going to slow down the 160 GW of backlog/demand power through 2029 vs. ~80 GW-100 GW of capacity build out planned the next few years. This technology wave will continue at high speed and the Blue Wave, bears, China hawks are not stopping this 4th Industrial Revolution."
In a separate post, Ives highlighted Apple (AAPL), cybersecurity players such as CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Palo Alto Networks (PANW), hyperscalers Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL), software firms Palantir (PLTR) and Snowflake (SNOW), and SpaceX (SPCX) as the possible beneficiaries in the tech market.
AI giant Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq on Thursday after a blockbuster IPO. However, after 17% opening day gains, the stock quickly lost steam. Investors pouring billions into the IPO, potentially diverting liquidity from other investments, was cited as one of the reasons behind last week's broader tech selloff.
Meanwhile, they are also closely watching the updates for Nvidia after the ouster of former CEO Jensen Huang and risks from multiple investigations into the AI chipmaker's dealings. Last week, Califonia opened a probe, while Nvidia said it did not plan to reinstate Huang.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday that no further restrictions on the sale of older Nvidia chips to China are needed following the Trump administration's move earlier this week to block China's remote access to the latest semiconductors.
Nvidia's investments and partnerships span dozens of tech companies, making it central to the health of the AI industry. The spy scandal emerged as investors were already questioning the pace of AI spending and the market rally it had fueled.
On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment was 'extremely bullish' for NVDA, 'bullish' for AMD, MU and SNDK, 'bearish' for INTC and SOXX.

Another wrote , "$SOXX Get ready for V shape recovery."

articles.title_orig: Wall Street analysts cheer Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — but they still have concerns
articles.title_zh: Wall Street analysts cheer Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — but they still have concerns
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Bernstein analysts were quick to upgrade Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Monday after the board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO of the AI chipmaker, though Wall Street sees ongoing investigations as a lingering overhang on the company.
The stock surged as much as 32% following Huang's reinstatement. President Trump said he spoke to the board and "convinced" them to reinstate Huang.
Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon and his team, which had downgraded the stock to a Neutral-equivalent Market Perform rating just 11 days ago, rerated the stock as Outperform as soon as the board announced Huang's return.
"As we remain positive on AI buildout fundamentals, and with Jensen back in the seat, we upgrade today back to [Outperform] (as his exit was the primary reason for the downgrade)," Rasgon wrote.
The analyst maintained a $200 price target, highlighting questions that will likely leave some overhang in place, including ongoing investigations which may limit NVDA's multiple for now.
"While we are happy to have Jensen back, the on-again-off-again response from the board is, frankly, clown-like," the analysts added, questioning what this says about how the board goes about making other decisions.
Yorkville's Dan Ives, which has maintained a Buy rating on the stock, said on Monday that the firm believes Nvidia stock should be valued at $300 with Jensen Huang back. However, the analysts kept $225 as the price target for the stock, saying they're looking for a resolution of the board's investigation.
The path to closing the price gap "runs through the committee's conclusion, a clean read on the export probe, and a 4Q print delivered by a CEO whose tenure is no longer a topic on the earnings call," Ives wrote.
KeyBank analyst John Vinh stated that while Jensen Huang's reinstatement is a "significantly positive development," the firm retains a Sector Weight, or Neutral, rating and awaits further clarification on the board's ongoing investigation and the SEC accounting inquiry before revisiting its rating,
Stifel analyst Ruben Roy, meanwhile, reiterated a Buy rating and maintained a $205 price target, noting that while Huang's return removes key-person risk, the ongoing investigations remain a potential overhang on the shares.
Several other analysts echoed the sentiment that a major overhang has been cleared, even as governance questions remain. In other words,
"In our view, the reinstatement removes the key overhang created by the CEO transition," Citi analyst Atif Malik wrote, issuing a Buy rating and raising the firm's price target to $240.
Malik noted that while Huang's reinstatement "restores continuity across NVDA's product roadmap," uncertainty remains around the scrutiny into Huang's relationships. "That said, we would view clean resolutions of these concerns as a further catalyst," Malik added.
Others pointed toward Nvidia shares responding to an overcorrection in selling.
Analyst Tristan Gerra noted that while Baird retained its Neutral rating, "near-term the stock has over-corrected and we expect a rerating towards our price target driven by the return of Mr. Huang as CEO."
"I am still a buyer of Nvidia today," Antoine Chkaiban, New Street Research analyst, said on Sozzi Unleashed . "I think there's still plenty of upside with the stock. It's still very cheap. You know we have Nvidia generating 25 bucks of earnings in 2028. So the stock is still trading below ten times that [on a PE ratio]. And I think there's plenty of upside."
Correction: A previous version of this article misstated Stifel's price target. We regret the error.

articles.title_orig: AI Mode adding Google Drive, Wallet, & Gemini app integration
articles.title_zh: AI Mode adding Google Drive, Wallet, & Gemini app integration
articles.content_orig:
Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.
By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.
Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.
As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.
Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.
Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.
The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

articles.title_orig: China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow
articles.title_zh: China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow
articles.content_orig:
China is preparing a major display of its expanding naval combat capabilities at Airshow China 2026 , with the carrier-based J-35 stealth fighter, Z-20F anti-submarine warfare helicopter and KJ-600 airborne early warning aircraft making their exhibition debuts.
The 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition will run from December 7–13 at the Zhuhai International Airshow Center in Guangdong, with public days scheduled for December 11–13. The PLA Navy announced its participation lineup on November 23.
Carrier aviation takes center stage
The J-35, J-15T, KJ-600, JL-15 trainer and Z-20J and Z-8C helicopters will participate in flight demonstrations featuring formation flypasts, low-level passes and simulated airfield strike drills.
The Z-20F will make its first-ever airshow appearance and public unveiling. The KJ-600, designed for airborne early warning and control (AEW&C), will also make its Airshow China debut.
"J-35, KJ-600 and Z-20F are all making their debut at the Airshow China. Among them, the Z-20F carrier-based anti-submarine helicopter is appearing at an airshow for the first time and being unveiled to the public for the very first time. This marks the public debut of all five domestically developed carrier-related assets ," Zhang Junshe, a military affairs expert told the Global Times on Monday.
Designed for catapult-assisted takeoff and arrested recovery (CATOBAR), the KJ-600 has already conducted electromagnetic catapult launches and arrested landings aboard China's Type 003 aircraft carrier, Fujian. It previously appeared publicly during the September 2025 military parade in Beijing.
The exhibition will also feature the J-15DT electronic warfare fighter, Y-9 anti-submarine patrol aircraft and WZ-2 unmanned helicopter.
Together, the J-35, J-15T, KJ-600, J-15DT and Z-20F represent five key carrier-related platforms covering fighter operations, electronic warfare, airborne surveillance and anti-submarine warfare.
The land-based J-35A made its public flight debut at Airshow China 2024, while AVIC has also promoted the J-35 platform internationally, including at the Dubai and Singapore airshows.
Three major warships make their debut
For the first time, Airshow China will feature a dedicated maritime exhibition zone at Gaolan Port, where visitors can tour three active-duty warships: the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, Type 055 guided-missile destroyer and Type 054A guided-missile frigate.
All three vessels are making their Airshow China debut.
The Type 055, a 10,000-ton-class destroyer, is a major surface combatant associated with China's carrier strike groups. Its public ship tour is among the exhibition's principal attractions.
This year, the Navy also plans to showcase three classes of major warships and nearly ten aircraft types through indoor exhibitions, outdoor static displays, flight demonstrations and vessel tours.
Unmanned aerial and underwater systems will also feature prominently.
The expanded showcase brings carrier-based aviation, surface combatants, amphibious warfare assets and unmanned technologies together in a single exhibition, offering a high-profile display of China's ongoing naval modernization.

articles.title_orig: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
articles.title_zh: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
articles.content_orig:
Some may have found it ironic that the world's biggest conference on climate change should collapse over the very mention of fossil fuels - the main cause of global warming.
Yet that is what happened in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.
The failure tells us something about the state of climate diplomacy. But it may tell us even more about the increasingly divided world in which the negotiations take place.
Chris Bowen, the Australian minister who led the negotiations, spoke of a backdrop constituting "the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory". The competing demands, he said, had become "unbridgeable red lines".
Murat Kurum, Turkey's environment minister and the summit's president, was blunter. Governments should not disappoint people desperate for climate action, he suggested, by getting "hung up on one word or phrase".
And Kurum had a point. Three years ago, at COP28 in Dubai, there was agreement to transition away from fossil fuels. The proposed Antalya Pact failed to mention them at all.
Was it really worth sacrificing the agreement over two words, then?
The countries that rejected it said the distinction was fundamental. They argued that there was a world of difference between promising to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and committing to move away from the fuels responsible for most of them. Without that explicit commitment, they feared the new agreement would weaken the one made in Dubai.
Normally, it is difficult to establish exactly who has said what at these conferences. Much of the bargaining takes place behind closed doors, and governments are often reluctant to admit which proposals they have opposed.
This time, some of the opposition was public - mostly from oil-producing nations.
Mohammad Ayoub, a Saudi negotiator speaking on behalf of the 22 Arab League countries, argued that Arab nations had contributed less than 2% of historical greenhouse gas emissions. It was wealthy industrialised nations, he said, that bore the overwhelming responsibility for the problem.
He defended the Arab countries' right to choose how to tackle climate change according to their national circumstances.
Russia's delegate Sergei Kononuchenko went further. Cutting oil and gas supplies before demand fell, he warned, would cause shortages, higher prices and energy poverty.
"For that reason, we cannot agree to any formulation on fossil fuel," he said.
The wider political backdrop was still more revealing.
The US, which in previous rounds of talks had helped broker compromises - sometimes working alongside China - had no official delegation in Antalya. President Donald Trump has rejected the entire international climate process.
And while delegates argued over fossil fuels in Turkey, Trump, China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin issued a joint declaration in Shenzhen that included a pledge to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products.
The priorities of some of the world's most powerful governments appeared very different from those being discussed in the negotiating rooms.
Yet, perhaps, the picture is more optimistic than it first appears. About 130 governments backed a demand for explicit language on moving away from fossil fuels - roughly two-thirds of the countries represented in Antalya.
Christiana Figueres, who led the UN negotiations that delivered the Paris Agreement, argued that countries were right to walk away rather than endorse a weaker political commitment that might undermine the progress already made.
Looked at this way, the collapse is not evidence that the world has lost its appetite for climate action. Quite the opposite - a substantial majority of governments were demanding more ambitious action.
So why not simply find a way for them to move ahead without waiting for the countries determined to block them?
The difficulty becomes clearer when you look beyond the dispute over fossil fuels.
Kononuchenko had another target in his sights: climate finance. Much of the money wealthy countries provide to poorer nations, he complained, comes as loans rather than grants. He said that developing countries ended up repaying more than they received.
"This is an old colonial distribution of labour under a new banner," he declared.
Then, in a striking moment, he leaned towards the microphone and switched from Russian into English to address his criticism directly to the Europeans: "First of all distinguished representatives of the EU."
Russia has its own reasons for attacking Europe, but the complaint about finance is one that many developing countries share. They argue that they are being asked to pay for damage they did little to cause while receiving too little help to adapt to climate change or build cleaner economies.
The EU had ruled out significant new funding before the negotiations began. Mohamed Adow, the Kenyan campaigner who heads Power Shift Africa, accused Europe of rejecting a flawed deal while refusing to acknowledge its own responsibility for the failure on finance.
So is it possible for a majority of countries to outvote those blocking progress?
The UN climate chief, Simon Stiell, has acknowledged the need to "improve, modernise and reform" the process. Some governments have proposed introducing voting when consensus proves impossible. Others want countries prepared to move faster to make their own agreements outside the formal talks.
But there is a reason the UN climate process depends on consensus. International climate co-operation is largely voluntary.
Voting might produce more ambitious agreements on paper, but would it persuade the governments that had been outvoted to act? Consensus also offers some protection to smaller and poorer nations that might otherwise find themselves overruled by the most powerful countries.
Meanwhile, the failure to agree a summit declaration does not mean climate action stops. Solar panels, batteries and electric vehicles are becoming increasingly competitive, while the upheaval in global oil and gas supplies is giving countries another reason to generate their own electricity rather than depend on imported fossil fuels.
The energy transition is moving forward, whatever happens in the UN negotiating rooms. The problem is that it is not moving nearly fast enough for the climate.
Perhaps the most poignant aspect of the failed Antalya Pact is what the countries had apparently been prepared to accept.
The final draft expressed "deep concern" that global warming was expected to exceed 1.5°C in the next few years. It warned that further warming would cause increasingly serious damage, some of it irreversible, and called for urgent action to limit how far temperatures rose above that threshold.
This remarkably strong language had survived into the final version, apparently without provoking the opposition that sank the agreement. Even countries bitterly divided over fossil fuels and finance seemed prepared to acknowledge the scale of the danger.
Yet they couldn't agree on how to respond.
And that, perhaps, is what Antalya tells us about the state of international climate co-operation. The problem isn't simply finding the right words or changing the voting rules. It is persuading countries with very different interests to take action that no international authority can compel them to take.
That was always going to be difficult. In today's divided world, it looks harder than ever.

The countdown is officially here: there are only four days until Black Friday 2026 . That doesn’t mean you should wait to shop, however. Amazon , Walmart , Home Depot , Apple , PlayStation , Alo , Hoka , Nintendo and more already rolled out deals, and at this point, once a product’s price drops, you can be pretty confident that it’s the best offer you’ll see.
I’ve spent over six years covering major sales as a reporter and on-air correspondent for NBC Selected. I’ve been tracking prices for weeks and combing through thousands of discounts to find the best Black Friday deals actually worth buying . Each one I recommend below is highly rated and 20 percent off or more. When possible, I also ran deals through price trackers like CamelCamelCamel to make sure they’re at their lowest price in at least three months — I even found seven that are currently at their lowest price ever. I’m updating this live today, November 23, with my expert-approved picks, so save this link and check back in often.

I use my AirPods Pro 3 every day to listen to music, take calls and watch TV. I’m always impressed by how much noise they block while I’m commuting or at the gym, and I appreciate the ability to use transparency mode when I want to be aware of my surroundings. The earbuds also have built-in heart rate sensing, live language translation, hearing aid and hearing test features. They come with five sets of ear tips in different sizes, which lets you customize their fit, and a charging case that extends their battery life.
Hoka ’s Arahi sneakers are one of our favorite pairs, and since the brand recently released the ninth edition, the previous one is currently on sale. Hoka made minimal changes between the models, so it’s worth buying the Arahi 8 if you need a solid walking or running shoe . It has a built-in stability system that helps prevent overpronation, and a moderate layer of soft cushioning to absorb shock and keep your feet comfortable. The sneakers come in regular and wide styles, and men’s and women’s sizes.

articles.title_orig: Israeli Political Leaders Denounce ‘Jewish Terrorism’ After West Bank Attacks
articles.title_zh: Israeli Political Leaders Denounce ‘Jewish Terrorism’ After West Bank Attacks
articles.content_orig:
Israeli settlers have attacked several Palestinian towns and villages in the central occupied West Bank, burning cars and damaging property.
The attacks early on Sunday included the burning of 12 vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on the walls of homes in Ramallah and el-Bireh provinces, reported the Palestinian news agency Wafa. The incidents were reported in Kafr Malik village, Deir Abu Mash’al village, and Deir al-Sudan village.
“Residents were awakened around two in the morning by sounds of fire and explosions. They realised the settlers had set fire to cars,” reported Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh from Kafr Malik.
Israeli settler violence has surged across the occupied West Bank since Israel launched its genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza. At least 1,222 people, including 255 children, have been killed in attacks there since Israel launched its war in October 2023 in response to the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel.
The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission said there was a significant increase in the number of attacks throughout the Palestinian territory last month.
According to the Palestinian Authority body, there were 3,133 attacks in October, with Israeli forces responsible for 1,764 of them and Israeli settlers 1,369.
The commission said the total number of attacks increased by 53 percent compared with September when 2,051 attacks were recorded. Settler attacks alone rose from 647 in September to 1,369 in October – a 112 percent increase.
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar Party, who has been tasked with forming a new government after Israel’s general election last month, criticised the latest attacks on Sunday.
He wrote on social media that the attacks were “Jewish terrorism in every sense of the word, and it must be called what it is”.
“Sabotage by extremist groups setting fire to vehicles and homes undermines regional stability, endangers lives and severely damages the national security of the state of Israel and its foreign relations,” he posted on X.
“The actions led by Ben-Gvir and Smotrich in the West Bank have brought the area to the brink of unchecked anarchy,” he added, referring to far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.
Ben-Gvir rejected the allegations and said Eisenkot was rushing to conclusions. He wrote on social media that Eisenkot’s stance represents a “down payment” to Arab Knesset member Ahmad Tibi in preparation for forming a government with the support of Arab parties.
Settlers are often “escorted by Israeli squads and they do nothing to stop the attackers,” Shai Parnes of the Israeli human rights organisation B’Tselem told Al Jazeera.
The Israeli military said it was sending police officers and investigators from the Criminal Identification Unit to the attacked areas “to collect evidence as part of the ongoing investigation”, the military wrote on social media.

articles.title_orig: Amazon snaps up Decart's AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
articles.title_zh: Amazon snaps up Decart's AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
articles.content_orig:
Amazon is scooping up much of the technology and talent behind artificial intelligence startup Decart, marking the latest reverse acquihire deal by a major tech company.
In a Monday blog post , Amazon said it agreed to purchase Decart's "proprietary technology" and hire the startup's three founders, as well as their AI researchers and engineers.
The Israeli startup, founded in 2023, is best known for its software that lets developers sync their AI models across different chips, allowing them to switch hardware quickly, known as the Decart Optimization Stack.
"Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip," Peter DeSantis, a senior vice president at Amazon who oversees foundation models, custom silicon and quantum computing development, said in a statement. "More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost."
DeSantis added, "From our earliest work with Decart, we knew they were the kind of technologically fearless team who would help us push it even further."
Amazon has moved deeper into building custom AI chips amid insatiable demand for the technology, and as companies seek alternatives to Nvidia , the dominant provider. Amazon has positioned its Trainium and Inferentia chips as lower-cost options for AI developers.
Last month, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said the company plans to make its Trainium chips externally available for the first time in "late in 2027."
Several outlets reported Amazon will pay $7.5 billion for Decart's assets, citing people familiar with the matter. Amazon declined to comment on the terms of the deal.
Anthropic had considered acquiring Decart and conducted due diligence, but ultimately walked away from a deal, Bloomberg reported.
Tech companies including Microsoft , Meta and Google have announced a series of deals with buzzy AI startups, which involve licensing their technology or nabbing their top talent and founders. The moves, often referred to as reverse acquihires , stop short of buying the companies outright. Amazon made two similar deals in 2024 when it brought on talent from Adept and Covariant .
The arrangements have attracted regulatory scrutiny in some cases. Amazon said Monday the Decart deal is subject to regulatory approval.

articles.title_orig: AI rally set to add $2 trillion to Nasdaq-100 as Huang returns to Nvidia helm
articles.title_zh: AI rally set to add $2 trillion to Nasdaq-100 as Huang returns to Nvidia helm
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Wall Street spent last week dumping anything tied to AI. It's spending Monday buying it back.
The Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), the fund that tracks the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ), opened almost 8% higher, its biggest jump at the open since it launched in 1999. Its closest rivals for largest jumps came in 2000 and 2001 as the dot-com bubble was bursting and big rallies had a habit of fizzling.
The SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) opened 5% higher. Among Mondays since 1993, only Oct. 13, 2008, in the depths of the financial crisis, started with a bigger jump.
The rally is holding. By midday, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) is up more than 4% and on track for its best day since April 2025, the Nasdaq-100 is up more than 6%, and the CBOE Volatility Index ( ^VIX ) is down about 8 points.
The surge comes as Nvidia ( NVDA ) brought back Jensen Huang as CEO and after the S&P 500 slid into a correction last week.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) opened 15% higher, its biggest jump at the open since it launched in 2001 and well past its previous record of about 9% in October 2002.
Nvidia opened up 33% on Huang's return and is on track for one of the best days in the company's history, which tops out at a 42% gain in March 2000. Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ), Micron ( MU ), and AMD ( AMD ) opened roughly 12% to 21% higher.
Read more: Buy Nvidia stock or wait? A guide to making the call on any stock.
Not everyone thinks the panic has run its course. Options sentiment "screams" the worst levels since the pandemic and Liberation Day, Roundhill Investments chief investment strategist Drew Pettit told Yahoo Finance, "but it's not a washout."
History sides with the bulls, eventually. In the 20 times since 1993 that SPY opened Monday 2% or more higher, it was higher a year later in 17 of those, with a median gain of about 25%, roughly double that of a typical year, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
Creative Planning's Charlie Bilello found a similar pattern . Last week's nearly 9% drop was the S&P 500's 12th-worst week since 1950, he noted, and after the worst weeks, stocks averaged a 26% gain over the next year, compared with 11% otherwise.
Evercore ISI's Julian Emanuel is in that camp too, writing over the weekend, "Bull Market intact as double-digit EPS gains likely ahead."
In half of those 20 cases, SPY slipped back below the prior Friday's low within three months, most often within two weeks. Think of it as the morning after a big night out. The headache usually comes back before it goes away.
Even so, eight of those 10 were higher a year later. The two closest matches to this setup, October 2008 and May 2010, each paired a brutal week with a big Monday open, sank further over the next three months and were about 15% higher a year later.
That puts Friday's low, about 6,883 on the S&P 500, in focus. And the Fed isn't riding to the rescue , with Wall Street still pricing a December rate hike and every correction that hits with inflation speeding up this fast turning into a bear market .
BTIG's strategists aren't calling a bottom yet. "We don't think this is the final low, but we are looking for a short-term rally back towards 7250-7350 before likely turning lower again," they wrote over the weekend.
As of midday Monday, the S&P 500 is already knocking on the bottom of that range.

articles.content_orig:
Update [ Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 2:50pm ]: Well, the patch notes are out! Rockstar Games mentions seven official fixes for the update, and none of them are specifically to do with the Xbox Series S or other things like how bright the game is.
Nevertheless, there's always a chance they've made some extra tweaks under the hood.
Here are the official seven fixes in GTA 6's first post-launch update (November 23):
Original Story: GTA 6 only officially launched late last week, but Rockstar Games has already pushed out a new update (01.002.002) for the game across Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S (along with PS5), rolling out as of a few hours ago.
You're looking at a download size of around 1.6GB for update 1.0.2 on Xbox Series X and S.
In terms of what's included, Rockstar has yet to issue any official patch notes, and we'll have to wait and see whether anything is distributed. We'll obviously update this article with the patch notes if they're made available to us.
Players are trying to make their own discoveries in the meantime, with suggestions that the game may run smoother on Xbox Series S now, that saving your game returns you to the exact same spot instead of your safehouse (although this seemed to be happening for us already), and that the first-person glitch is still working as things stand.
All of these could be akin to placebo effects though, so take them with a pinch of salt:
As you can see from one of the impressions above, there's a suggestion that the game seems brighter now, which perhaps could have something to do with the borked HDR calibration tool that we discussed the other day .
That said, who knows whether these are areas that have actually been targeted for the update, or whether they're just happy coincidences that some players are experiencing. In any case, we'll keep an eye out for any official confirmations.
